scope: Isolated S1 reload from a crash page that history rebuilt. A second failure closes a crash page left in history, and back rebuilds it in a new pipeline. No product dependency or runtime configuration changes.
owner_decisions: Patch servo-net so request interception cannot replace a crash error page (2026-11-26).
An error page is recoverable by navigating back, reloading, or editing the target URL (2026-11-24).

baseline.head: b2cacaf
baseline.note: The crash page evidence records three passing runs in each mode at this checkpoint. origin/main was also at b2cacaf when this work started.

configuration.crash_page_check: Each fetched crash document must contain the engine's failure reason. Servo's crash.html embeds that reason. The check only orders the fixture and grants no host authority.

changes.name: Reload from a rebuilt crash page inherited its sandboxing
changes.observed: The constellation stored the failed document's load data under the crash pipeline's id and removed it when that pipeline exited. A crash page can stay in history. A later failure in the same view closes every history pipeline and marks each entry for reload with its load data. Back then rebuilds the crash page in a new pipeline with no stored record, so reload went to the crash page's script thread again. The reloaded document had an opaque origin and no scripts in both modes.
changes.fix: The crash page's load data now carries the creation sandboxing flags of the load that it replaced. History keeps that load data, so it survives eviction and recovery. Reload of a pipeline whose load data has crash details replaces it through the constellation with that load: crash details removed, original flags restored, and the reload-navigation flag set. The pipeline-keyed record is removed.

findings: Back to a closed crash entry rebuilds Servo's error page with the original failure reason in both modes.
Reload from the rebuilt error page restores the failed document with its real origin and running scripts.
The reload now sets the reload-navigation flag and clears the history-navigation flag, as a script-thread reload does. The previous record reused the failed load's flags unchanged.

single_process.scope: Experimental engine scope, host allocation gate, script-thread unwind, final-handle release, explicit engine shutdown, queued execution cancellation, interruption of running JavaScript, content-process exit and forced kill in multiprocess mode, shared-process view revocation and ordinary sibling close, script-thread failure and content-process exit or kill before document construction, crash recovery through reload and history, callback and delegate unwind safety, and constellation loss in a separate engine. Remaining replacement audits remain open.

local_validation.patch_reproduction: The patch applies to the seven published packages with patch -F 0 and no offsets. A fresh application reproduces the development sources byte for byte.
local_validation.binary_isolation: Each run used a private copy of its binary. The negative control was built before the fix. The final binary matches the SHA-256 of both passing final reports.
local_validation.product_changes: None. Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, product crates, and installed natives are unchanged.

limitations: Multiprocess evidence uses unsandboxed children on macOS arm64 with software rendering.
The crash reload replacement uses default target snapshot parameters. A view that started with sandboxing from its opener or a frame would lose those flags on reload. No fixture covers that case.
The fixture rebuilds a crash entry only through a second failure in the same view. History eviction and document discard use the same load data path but are not exercised.
Crash pages for about:blank documents remain blank.
Nested browsing-context history after crash recovery remains unchecked.
No new Linux, native-input, release-performance, or remote CI evidence is claimed.
